events.audience: Open to the university community; some talks restricted to graduate students and faculty
events.source_note: Twelve dated talks from January 2025 to April 2026. As with the lecture series, the cadence is inferred from the spacing of instances rather than stated. Held in TASC 1 9204 on Burnaby campus.

events.name: Computing Science Student Society board game nights
events.cadence: Every other Friday during term
events.audience: Open social event for Computing Science students
events.source_note: The society books TASC 9204 on Burnaby campus and provides food. One of the few club events with a stated room.

events.name: Computing Science Student Society general meetings
events.cadence: Every two weeks during term
events.audience: Computing Science students and society members
events.source_note: Listed under the society own Regular Events heading. No room or campus is stated for the meeting itself.

events.name: CSSS Silicon Valley Trip
events.cadence: Annually
events.audience: Computing Science students, organised by the Computing Science Student Society
events.source_note: Listed under the society's yearly events: every year, a group heads to California. No dates, cost, or itinerary are published on the page, and no dated instance was found, so recurrence rests on the society's own statement. Meetup is the least-wrong format value; the enum has no travel category.

events.name: eCo-op Coffee Chat
events.cadence: Once per semester; a fall session is listed for Thursday 22 October
events.audience: Students considering the Entrepreneurship Co-op or eGrad programs; hosted by current eCo-op students
events.source_note: The page states a casual coffee chat is hosted once each semester. Held on Burnaby campus with the room listed as TBD, so the zone is the campus catch-all. The listed date carries no year on the page.

events.name: Engineering Science Student Society general meetings
events.cadence: Bi-weekly during term, alternating with executive meetings
events.audience: Open to anyone; voting rights for students in engineering science majors, minors, or classes
events.source_note: Both the general and executive meeting times read TBD for Spring 2026 on the society own page. The society office address appears in every page footer, so it is not evidence of where meetings are held.

events.name: Fall Hacks
events.cadence: Annually in the fall term; the 2026 edition on 7 November is the sixth
events.audience: SFU students, beginner-first, returning participants welcome
events.source_note: Run by the Computing Science Student Society as a 12-hour sprint. The site states 2026 is the sixth edition hosted at SFU. Sign-in at the Applied Science Building entrance on Burnaby campus.

events.name: Founders Circle
events.cadence: Weekly on Mondays, 3:30-4:30 PM, except statutory holidays; the Fall 2026 series runs to 14 December
events.audience: Innovators of all experience levels; hosted by a Chang Institute Mentor-in-Residence
events.source_note: Discussion group on assigned podcasts and readings about founders, run by a Chang Mentor-in-Residence. Virtual or in person at Surrey campus room SRYC 4355. Dated Fall 2026 sessions are published from 21 September through 14 December.

events.name: ICPC North America Pacific Northwest Regional at SFU
events.cadence: Annually in November; SFU hosted the Canadian site in 2024 and 2025
events.audience: University teams from across the region, eligible under ICPC rules
events.source_note: SFU hosts a site of a regional contest rather than owning the event. Two consecutive years are established: UBC records its teams competing at SFU in November 2024, and SFU ran the November 2025 edition. The 2026 date is set but the site list is not published, so SFU is a repeat host rather than a confirmed 2026 one. Held in the Applied Science Building.

events.name: JourneyHacks
events.cadence: Annually in January or February; 10 January 2026 and 14 February 2025
events.audience: Beginners; college and university students
events.source_note: SFU Surge beginner-friendly counterpart to StormHacks. Edition pages for 2024, 2025 and 2026. Held on Burnaby campus.

events.name: Mountain Madness
events.cadence: Annually in the spring term; the 2026 edition ran 28 February to 1 March
events.audience: Students of all skill levels, including first years
events.source_note: Run by the Computing Science Student Society as a 24-hour marathon. Edition pages resolve for 2018, 2021, 2024, 2025 and 2026; the run is established as recurring rather than unbroken. Registration in front of SSCC 9001 on Burnaby campus.

events.name: OpFair
events.cadence: Annually; the 2026 edition ran 25-26 March and the next is advertised for January 2027
events.audience: All Faculty of Applied Sciences students
events.source_note: Run by the Engineering Science Student Society, which calls it SFU largest tech-based career fair. Its own site states it has run since 1993, across 31 fairs. SFU recruitment-fairs page independently lists it as annual and tech-focused. The 2026 edition ran in the Academic Quadrangle.

events.name: Opportunity Fest
events.cadence: Annually in November
events.audience: Entrepreneurial-minded students across SFU; open to everyone
events.source_note: The Chang Institute calls it SFU largest showcase of student entrepreneurship projects. The 2025 edition was 25 November at the SFU Surrey Mezzanine; a 2026 November edition is referenced by the Fall 2026 entrepreneurship course but has no published date.

events.name: Pi Week
events.cadence: Annually, the week of 14 March
events.audience: SFU engineering students
events.source_note: Run by the Engineering Science Student Society. The society states the events each day of the week change every year, so the week recurs while its contents do not. The society rebuilt its site in 2026 and the old annual-events page returns 404; the entry follows the live events page.

events.name: SFU Engineering Competition
events.cadence: Annually, roughly at the start of November
events.audience: SFU engineering students
events.source_note: Organized by the ESSS, MSESS, and SEESS, per the ESSS conferences and competitions page. The society rebuilt its site in 2026 and the old annual-events page, which described the event as the official qualifier for the Western Engineering Competition, returns 404; the rebuilt page does not repeat that claim, so it is no longer asserted here.

events.name: SFU OS Dev Club speaker series
events.cadence: Monthly during term
events.audience: Club members and students interested in open source
events.source_note: Two consecutive monthly instances are documented, titled February and March speaker series, each with its own write-up. The year is not stated on either. Filed against the site root rather than its events page: sfuosdev.com/events is a client-side route that returns 404 to a direct request while rendering normally in a browser, so it is not a citable address.

events.name: SIAT end-of-term showcases
events.cadence: Every term, at the end of the fall, spring, and summer terms
events.audience: Open to the public; attendees playtest student projects and give feedback
events.source_note: A cluster of per-course showcases under one banner across a few weeks rather than a single dated event, held across Surrey campus rooms. Two in-person rounds are documented directly, Fall 2024 and Spring 2025; the term pages from Fall 2020 onward are project galleries and do not by themselves prove an in-person round each term. The linked page is the gallery, which is the durable address.

events.name: SparkJam
events.cadence: Recurs, but no page states a cadence; editions in 2025 and 2026
events.audience: Students working in brand, interface, motion, prototyping, and pitching
events.source_note: A two-week design sprint hosted by SFU Surge rather than a coding hackathon. Recurrence rests on artefacts rather than any statement: two separate deployments a year apart and two dated repositories. Neither a date, an eligibility rule, nor a venue is published anywhere reachable; the site is a client-rendered app whose HTML carries only metadata.

events.name: StormHacks
events.cadence: Annually in early October; editions in 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026
events.audience: Students, beginner friendly, in teams of one to four
events.source_note: SFU Surge calls it their flagship hackathon and its own site calls it West Canada largest. Five separate edition pages establish the run. The 2026 edition is 3-4 October on Burnaby campus; the 2023 edition was in May, so the October timing is recent rather than invariant.

events.name: SystemsFair
events.cadence: Annually in January; 14 January 2026 and 17 January 2025
events.audience: Engineering students based on the Surrey campus: mechatronics, software systems, and sustainable energy
events.source_note: Run by the Mechatronic Systems Engineering Student Society with the software systems and sustainable energy societies. Corrected from Burnaby: it is a Surrey-campus fair. Not filed against systemsfair.ca, the address still surfacing in search results, which returns 404 from Wix.

events.name: Tech Fair
events.cadence: Annually in autumn; the 2026 edition is 4 November
events.audience: Computing Science students
events.source_note: Run by the Computing Science Student Society. Per-edition pages resolve for 2022, 2023 and 2024 alongside the live 2026 site, and the site states it has been growing since 2022. Held in the Applied Sciences Building on Burnaby campus.

events.name: Try/CATCH
events.cadence: Annually in the autumn; editions in 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025
events.audience: High school girls and non-binary students in grades 8 to 12
events.source_note: An outreach event organised every year by Women in Computing Science, per SFU own page. Held on Burnaby campus, the 2025 edition in the Applied Sciences Building. A claim that it dates to 2009 appears in search results but on no page that could be fetched, so it is not asserted here.

events.name: WiCS and WiE Networking Night
events.cadence: Annually in January or February
events.audience: All students in SFU Faculty of Applied Sciences; mentors are women in technical roles
events.source_note: Run jointly by Women in Computing Science and Women in Engineering; panel followed by speed networking. The page states it is held every January or February, but the newest documented edition is 30 January 2024 and no 2025 or 2026 edition appears on it, so the gap is recorded rather than smoothed over. WiE's own page independently lists Networking Night among its events. No venue is published.

events.name: WiCS Lunch and Learn
events.cadence: Twice per semester: one lunch on Burnaby campus and one on Surrey
events.audience: Women in Computing Science students, four per lunch, with a female SFU CS faculty host
events.source_note: The page states every semester we have 1 lunch in Burnaby and 1 lunch in Surrey, and lists ten past lunches by faculty host. No instance is dated, so recurrence rests on the stated cadence and the length of the host list rather than on dated evidence.

events.name: Women In Engineering weekly meetings
events.cadence: Weekly during term, Thursdays 8:00 to 8:30 PM
events.audience: Women In Engineering members and newcomers at SFU
events.source_note: Cadence stated on the club own SFU-hosted page, which carries a page-updated stamp of 2026-07-08. Held on Discord rather than in a room, so the zone records the faculty rather than a location.

events.name: XHacks
events.cadence: Annually in late January; the 2026 edition ran 31 January to 1 February
events.audience: Beginner hackers; the 2026 edition reported more than 200 participants
events.source_note: Formerly SystemsHacks, run by the Software Systems Student Society, which describes the 2026 edition as its tenth annual hackathon and a decade of the event. One SFU listing calls XHacks 2026 first-ever, which refers to the new 24-hour format rather than the event.
